syllabusTopics: Logic and set: statements, logical connectives, truth tables, theorems based on set operations
Real numbers: geometric representation of real numbers, interval, absolute value
Function: domain and range of a function, inverse function, composite function; algebraic (linear, quadratic and cubic) and transcendental (trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic) functions

Curve sketching: odd and even functions, periodicity, symmetry (about origin, X- and Y-axis), monotonicity; graphs of quadratic, cubic and rational functions, trigonometric (asinbx and acosbx), exponential (e^x), logarithmic (lnx)
Sequence and series: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic sequences and series and their properties; A.M, G.M, H.M and their relations; sum of infinite geometric series
Matrices and determinants: transpose of a matrix and its properties; minors and cofactors, adjoint, inverse matrix, determinant, properties of determinants (without proof)
Quadratic equation: nature and roots of a quadratic equation, relation between roots and coefficient, formation of a quadratic equation, symmetric roots, one or both roots common
Complex number: imaginary unit, algebra of complex numbers, geometric representation, absolute (modulus) value and conjugate of complex numbers and their properties, square root of a complex number

card.title: Logic and set: statements, logical connectives, truth tab…

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Logic and sets share one grammar. A **statement** has a definite truth value; connectives build compound statements whose truth tables obey fixed conventions — crucially **p → q is false only for T→F** (vacuous truth elsewhere), and p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q. **Tautologies** are always true, contradictions always false.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q; ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q; ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q - |A∪B| = |A| + |B| − |A∩B|; |P(A)| = 2ⁿ - A∪(B∩C) = (A∪B)∩(A∪C); A∪(A∩B) = A; A∪A′ = U - a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a+b+c)(a²+b²+c²−ab−bc−ca)

rows.text: ❌ answer with no steps → ✅ show each step and box the result.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "(A u B)' = A' n B'; A u (B n C) = (A u B) n (A u C); p -> q is false only when p is true and q is false."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The dictionary*** — every tautology is a set identity wearing logic clothes: swap not/and/or for complement/intersection/union and the truth table becomes a membership table.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Logic Meets Sets Statements, connectives and truth tables are the grammar of reasoning; sets are the nouns the grammar talks about. The theorems: the **algebra of sets** — De Morgan's laws, distributive laws, absorption — proved by membership tables, with truth tables as the logical twin.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Statements and connectives - A **statement** is a declarative sentence that is definitively true or false. **Connectives:** ¬ (not), ∧ (and), ∨ (or), → (implies), ↔ (if and only if). - **Truth-table conventions:** ¬ flips T/F; p ∧ q is true only when both are true; p ∨ q is false only when both are false; **p → q is false only when p is T and q is F** (vacuously true otherwise); p…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Truth table of p -> q: only T,F,T,T. A - B = A n B'. Power set: 2^n. Set identities: membership table, 8 rows. a+b+c = 0 => a^3+b^3+c^3 = 3abc.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}, find A ∪ B, A ∩ B and A − B. (3m)** — **Union** — elements in at least one set: A∪B = **{1, 2, 3, 4}**. **Intersection** — elements common to both: A∩B = **{2, 3}**.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Prove that A ∪ (B ∩ C) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C). (3m)** — **Membership-table proof.** Every element x is in one of 8 patterns w.r.t. A, B, C. Build the columns: **B∩C** (T iff both T); **LHS = A∪(B∩C)**; **A∪B**; **A∪C**; **RHS = (A∪B)∩(A∪C)**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In membership-table proofs, label the columns and state "all rows agree, hence equal" - the concluding sentence carries the proof mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The membership table is a finite proof of an infinite statement: two sets are equal iff every one of the 8 membership patterns agrees on both sides.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Statement: definite truth value. Connectives: not, and, or, implies, iff; p -> q false only when p T and q F (vacuously true otherwise). Tautology (always true), contradiction (always false), contingency. Power set has 2^n members. Inclusion-exclusion: |A u B| = |A| + |B| - |A n B|.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: De Morgan's laws are the reason search engines understand "NOT (cats OR dogs)" as "(not cats) AND (not dogs)".

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ is equal to: (a) abc (b) 3abc (c) −abc (d) 0 (1m)** — **Key identity:** a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca).…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Statement** | Sentence with a definite truth value | "3 is prime" (T) | | **Tautology** | True under every assignment | p → p | | **Power set** | Set of all subsets | P({1,2}) has 4 members | | **De Morgan's laws** | Complement flips ∪/∩ | (A∪B)′ = A′∩B′ |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the membership table proves everything - Two sets are equal iff they contain exactly the same elements. Tabulating membership for every element-type (in/out of each of A, B, C) exhausts all cases — a finite proof of an infinite statement.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Connectives vs set operations** | Logic | Sets | Meaning | |---|---|---| | ¬p | A′ | not in | | p ∧ q | A∩B | in both | | p ∨ q | A∪B | in at least one | | p → q | A ⊆ B | membership transfers |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Show p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q by truth table.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **p → q with false p is true:** the only false case is T→F — students mark false antecedent rows wrong.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **A − B ≠ B − A:** difference is not commutative; A−B = A∩B′ is the working form.  ·  **De Morgan's flip:** complementing a union gives an intersection of complements — the connective changes too.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}, find A ∪ B, A ∩ B and A − B. (3m)** — **Union** (elements in either): A∪B = **{1, 2, 3, 4}**. **Intersection** (elements in both): A∩B = **{2, 3}**. **Difference** (in A, not in B): A−B = **{1}**.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Prove A ∪ (B ∩ C) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C). (3m)** — **Membership table** with rows for x in/out of A, B, C. Columns: B∩C (T only when both B, C are T); left A∪(B∩C); A∪B; A∪C; right (A∪B)∩(A∪C).…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Construct the truth table of p → q and (¬p) ∨ q and show they are logically equivalent.** — Rows (p, q): (T,T), (T,F), (F,T), (F,F). p→q: T, F, T, T. ¬p∨q: F→T gives T; T→F gives F; F→T gives T; F→F gives T — column T, F, T, T.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ equals: (1m)** — **Identity:** a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). With a + b + c = 0 the right side vanishes, so a³ + b³ + c³ = **3abc → option (b)**. (This is the algebra's most-quoted conditional identity.)
